module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Opposite
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Defs

/-!
# Right ideals

This file defines right ideals over a semiring.
-/

@[expose] public section

universe u

/-- A right ideal in a semiring `R` is an additive submonoid closed under multiplication on the
right. It is implemented as a submodule of the right regular module. -/
abbrev RightIdeal (R : Type u) [Semiring R] :=
  Submodule Rᵐᵒᵖ R

reformulations.difference: Right ideals are represented as left submodules `Submodule Rᵐᵒᵖ R`, rather than directly bundling an additive submonoid with right-multiplication closure. For rings, the usual definition asks for an additive subgroup.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The canonical action satisfies `MulOpposite.op r • x = x * r` definitionally. Thus the Submodule fields are exactly containment of zero, closure under addition, and closure under multiplication on the right by arbitrary elements of R. Conversely, these three conditions construct a RightIdeal with the specified carrier. Over a ring, closure under additive inverses follows from multiplication by -1. The scratch file proves the general carrier-level iff and also constructs inverse conversions between RightIdeal R and Ideal Rᵐᵒᵖ using op/unop.
